answer: The registry scores every identity on cost of replication, computed from the deposit it locked and the distinct subnets behind its attestations, and any submission below the fleet median is re-queued for a second panel before it can mine. Clones arrive with the same thin deposit and the same two subnets, so they sit at the bottom and get re-queued until the epoch closes. Queue depth reaches its zenith in the last hour, by design, and a farm that missed the first panel is stuck there. A real operator clears the second panel before dawn and collects the nectar while the clones are still in line.
